scope: Source-only review of the four additional checkbox ARIA bindings in frozen 21.x checkout. No repository/dependency writes, build, test, DOM, or accessibility-tree execution.

readiness_matrix.relevant_finding: The matrix identifies four additions to owned checkbox.html compared with tagged legacy checkbox HTML, and explicitly says this is an observable augmentation, not proof of defect or grounds for removal.

reviewed.head_note: The matrix itself records heads 7143c2df99c07aec75822c389cc0f0f72361304a (21.x) and 036b362c669c3ce0d60da2eb0e217e013c33eed2 (main); the physical checkout HEAD observed for this review is 801cbac757b7cdba26bce86fbabaef6e30d547d2. The reviewed current template and checkbox-base files were rehashed at this actual HEAD and match the matrix-reported physical hashes exactly. The matrix HEAD is retained as the matrix subject, not represented as current HEAD.

owned_template.target: The bindings are on the existing visually-hidden, focusable native input[type=checkbox], adjacent to its native checked/disabled/name/value properties and aria-label/labelledby/describedby bindings.

tagged_reference.comparison: Exact tagged template contains aria-label, aria-labelledby, and aria-describedby on the native input, followed directly by change/click handlers; it has none of the four reviewed bindings. Tagged src/material/legacy-checkbox/checkbox.ts SHA-256 is 072551993542bffeacc517777d2144cab604e174b0c38988811a3c94ab45b908 and contains none of ariaExpanded, ariaControls, or ariaOwns.

details: aria-expanded is an @Input alias using booleanAttribute and has default null; source comment says it is for a checkbox controlling visibility of another element.
aria-controls and aria-owns are nullable string inputs, each defaulting to null.
owned_input_declarations.native_mixed_state: The existing indeterminate setter calls _syncIndeterminate; that writes the same boolean to native input.indeterminate. The template additionally emits aria-checked=mixed only while indeterminate is true; it removes the explicit attribute otherwise, leaving native checked state in control.

reviewed_current_files_rechecked_at_actu.result: both hashes match the bytes reviewed and the readiness-matrix recorded template hash

provenance.author: Ryan Lester
provenance.subject: fix(21.x): port recent main product adaptations
provenance.commit_body: The commit says it ports recent main product adaptations, including checkbox, onto 21.x as a path port without changing the Angular 21 lockfile; it does not claim G01-G13.
provenance.exact_checkbox_hunk: The template diff adds the four listed bindings. The same commit adds ariaExpanded (booleanAttribute transform), ariaControls, ariaOwns and their comments to checkbox-base.ts. The matrix cites upstream ref f8fccef631565ec80acc67e7ea0a654e24be99d9, but that object is not available in this local Git object database; this review therefore does not assert its exact source hunk or intent.

installed_peer_reference.evidence: Installed Material 21 MatCheckbox template forwards aria-checked=mixed, aria-controls, aria-expanded and aria-owns to its native checkbox input. Its public declaration documents the three input properties and component metadata exposes them. The modern template is MDC-based and structurally differs from the owned legacy template; this establishes current-peer support, not Material-16 provenance or authorization to change the legacy contract.

semantics_and_assessment.meaning: Explicitly exposes the tri-state mixed state while the component is indeterminate. For checked/unchecked, the binding removes its ARIA attribute and relies on native input.checked. Owned source also keeps native input.indeterminate synchronized.
semantics_and_assessment.assessment: This is a deliberate redundant mixed-state exposure relative to the native indeterminate property; it matches the installed Material 21 template. No static evidence here establishes a defect.

semantics_and_assessment.meaning: An optional ID reference from the checkbox to the element(s) it controls. The nullable input defaults to null, so no relation is emitted unless a caller supplies one.
semantics_and_assessment.assessment: Applicability depends on the consuming control; source alone cannot prove that supplied IDs exist or match a controlled region.

semantics_and_assessment.meaning: An optional expanded/collapsed state, boolean-transformed and forwarded to the input. The null default removes the attribute; false and true can express collapsed and expanded states.
semantics_and_assessment.assessment: Only appropriate when the checkbox actually controls visibility/expansion, as its source comment says. It is distinct from the checkbox's checked state.

semantics_and_assessment.meaning: An optional ID reference that asserts accessible-tree ownership of referenced node(s); the nullable input defaults to null.
semantics_and_assessment.assessment: This can alter accessibility-tree parentage and should be supplied only when that relationship is intended and valid.

recommendation: Do not remove or alter these bindings solely because the Material 16 template lacks them. Preserve the frozen 21.x behavior pending an intentional compatibility decision and targeted DOM/AX validation. Treat aria-checked as the mixed-state case and controls/expanded/owns as opt-in relationships whose caller-provided IDs and state must be validated.
proposed_runtime_assertions_not_executed: With no optional relation inputs, confirm the native checkbox input has no aria-controls, aria-expanded, or aria-owns attributes; confirm it retains its accessible name and native checked/unchecked state.

With a real controlled region, confirm supplied aria-controls IDREF resolves to that region and aria-expanded false/true tracks its collapsed/visible state. Also assert checkbox checked state remains independently represented.

When indeterminate becomes true, assert input.indeterminate is true and aria-checked is 'mixed'; after clearing it, assert input.indeterminate is false, explicit aria-checked is absent, and native checked state is preserved.

If exercising aria-owns, use a fixture with actual target IDs and verify browser accessibility-tree ownership and absence of duplicate/orphaned nodes; do not treat attribute presence alone as accessibility proof.

Run the same assertions at the supported peer floors and inspect browser accessibility snapshots/axe output; exact spoken output should not be asserted because it varies by browser and assistive technology.
limits: Source review only. No component runtime, browser DOM, accessibility tree, screen reader, or minimum-peer tests were run.
The exact historical Material 16 source is authenticated locally; the cited upstream adaptation commit is not present locally, so the port's remote origin was not independently reconstructed.
Installed Material 21 evidence establishes support by the current parent but does not settle the Material 16 legacy public API contract.
